title: Plump and Bean, six ways each

cards.title: Plump and Bean, varied
cards.text: Six takes each on Plump and Bean, the two you picked. Tick any you like, even only the face or the body.
cards.why: The bodies change a little and the faces change more, from curious to sleepy to sharp, so you can see what each change to a face does. Whatever you pick sets how every character in the app gets drawn.
cards.details:
Twelve crows: six takes on Plump (1 to 6) and six on Bean (7 to 12). Number 1 and number 7 are round 9's own drawings, unchanged, so you have something to compare against. Same room, pose, light and size as round 9, so only the bird changes. Still all flat: flat colours, a shade or two, no outlines, no mouths.

What changes: the body a little (rounder or taller, a hint of a neck, the wing, tail, legs and feet, and which black: blue-black, charcoal, warm brown-black, green-black, or a lighter smoky grey), and the face more. On the face: how big the eyes are and how far apart, a dark eye or one with a white, how far down the lid comes and which way it slopes, a glint or none, a small feather brow over the eye, the eye's colour (dark, ochre or pale silver), the beak's length and thickness, and how much of the far eye peeks out. Each family runs from curious to sleepy to sharp. None grins or frowns: a lid only ever slopes down toward the back of the head, never toward the beak, since that reads cross.

1 Plump: round 9's, unchanged. Dark eyes in a thin blue ring, a glint, a level lid.
2 Button: curious. Bigger round dark eyes with no lid and a big glint, set a little further from the beak; a shorter beak; the far eye shows whole. Charcoal (a grey black) with a thin edge of light.
3 Drowse: sleepy. A heavy lid half way down, sloping toward the back of the head, with a faint line along it. A lower, wider body. Warm brown-black.
4 Keen: sharp. Smaller pale silver eyes, the pupil looking ahead, a level lid and a small feather brow; a longer, slimmer beak. Plump's blue-black with a thin edge of light.
5 Amber: warm and attentive. Bigger ochre eyes with a glint and a lid that curves with the eye; a shorter, thicker beak. Green-black with a green wing.
6 Smoke: alert. Eyes with a white and a big dark iris, a brow set higher; a short, deep beak. A lighter smoky body with a darker wing and tail.
7 Bean: round 9's, unchanged. White eyes, upright pupils, a lid a third of the way down.
8 Pip: curious. Tall dark eyes with a big glint, no white and no lid, set wider apart, so more of the far eye shows. A rounder body. Blue-black with a thin edge of light.
9 Nap: sleepy. White eyes with the lid half down, sloping toward the back, the pupils low; a blunter beak. Leaning further forward. Warm black.
10 Scout: sharp. Narrow white eyes with small pupils looking ahead, a small feather brow; a longer, slimmer beak. Taller, on a short neck, with longer legs. Green-black with a thin edge of light.
11 Honey: warm and attentive. White eyes with big ochre irises and a lid that curves with the eye. Round 9's body, so this is the one where only the face changed.
12 Moon: curious. Big pale silver eyes, the lid barely down. A rounder body, a bigger head, bigger feet. A lighter slate body with a darker wing.

The pictures on the front: each family at room size, the six faces of each family large and side by side, then all twelve at icon size. Last round both birds went dark and muddy on the blue wall when small. This round tries three fixes: a thin edge of light along the top (2, 4, 8 and 10), a warm brown-black that stands apart from the blue (3 and 9), or a lighter body with a darker wing (6 and 12). Those eight read at icon size. 5 and 11 half do, thanks to their ochre eyes, and 1 and 7 are unchanged.

My pick is 4, Keen. It keeps Plump's soft round build and its blue-black, so it's still the bird you picked, and the thin edge of light is the smallest change that fixes it on the wall when small. Its face is the calmest clever one here: a pale eye under a level lid, the pupil looking ahead, a small brow, no smile and no frown. That kind of face would carry over to any character. My second is 10, Scout: the same idea on Bean, with narrow white eyes looking ahead, a small brow and a longer beak, in a green-black with an edge of light that reads small.

Still weak: the edge of light is what makes 2, 4, 8 and 10 read small, but at full size it comes close to an outline along the back. If it reads that way to you, a lighter body (6, 12) or a warm black (3, 9) does the same job without it. 6 and 12 read best on the wall but are grey rather than black, the furthest from a crow here. 5 and 11 still go dark when small apart from the eye. The far eye is fiddly: on 6 and 10 it shows as a white crescent at the edge of the head that can look like a notch, and on 3 it's only a dark sliver. 2 and 8 are the nearest to cute, with big glints and no lids, and 8's tall eyes in a ring can look a bit like a toy. 3 and 9 are sleepy on purpose and can read a little unimpressed. The small brows on 4, 6 and 10 vanish at icon size.
